newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pension funds to draw 19-23 bln Ffr per yr.
newsitem.headline: French pension funds to draw 19-23 bln Ffr per yr.

text.p: French pension funds should draw between 19 billion and 23 billion francs a year in four to five years when the programme reaches cruising speed, France's banking association AFB said on Monday.

The AFB said the funds should draw about four billion francs in their first year. It said it based its prediction on expectations that about 60 percent of small and medium-sized businesses and 75 percent of large companies would open plans for their employees.

It said it expected half of labourers and 75 percent of white collar workers would contribute to plans, that companies contributions would be about 1.5 percent of salaries and that white collar employees would contribute between 1.5 percent and three percent of their salaries.
It also expects one quarter of workers whose companies do not start plans to contribute to outside plans.
Another survey published by AFB showed employees believe average monthly contributions to the pension funds would total 983 francs.
That contribution would be made up of 587 francs from the employee and 396 francs from the company.
The French parliament adopted last week a law creating the pension funds, which should go into effect before the end of the year.
